source: Create a detailed Titanic-inspired ocean liner hull for a showcase. Make the ship very long and proportionally accurate, with a pointed bow, rounded stern, black lower hull, red underwater hull, and white upper hull. Use separate Parts/Models for major sections so I can edit them later. Do not create the interior yet.

answers.ask: How long should the hull be in studs? Titanic proportions come out around 900 studs, which is a wide frame for one image.
answers.answer: Use a smaller but still very long showcase scale of about 500 studs overall, preserving Titanic-like proportions.

answers.ask: Do players walk the decks of this showcase, or is the ship an object to be viewed from outside only?
answers.answer: This is an exterior showcase object viewed from outside only; do not build playable deck access or an interior yet.

scene_prompt: Create a detailed exterior showcase model of a Titanic-inspired ocean-liner hull, about 500 studs long and preserving the ship’s long, proportionally accurate profile. Form a pointed bow at one end and a rounded stern at the other, with a red underwater hull, black lower hull above the waterline, and white upper hull. Divide the exterior into separate editable Parts/Models for the major hull sections; leave out the interior and any playable deck access.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Entertainment (Showcase & Hub): this is an exterior object intended to be viewed, not traversed or played.

### Shape and preset
Use `set-display`, matching the Display Piece preset. The ocean liner is the single framed subject, with no walkable deck route, interior, or surrounding gameplay space.

### Config requirements
Use `landmark-focal` for the Titanic-inspired liner itself, composed as the sole hero object. No other image configuration options apply: water, a dock, visitors, interiors, and deck access were not requested.

### Layout requirements
No traversal, spawn, pickup, trigger, or emitter placement is needed. The ship is operated and viewed from outside only.

### Layout components
Build one approximately 500-stud-long ocean-liner hull on a neutral display ground or unobtrusive studio backdrop. Keep the silhouette long and proportionally Titanic-like: a sharply pointed bow at one end, a broad rounded stern at the other, and a continuous hull taper between them. Divide the visible exterior into editable major Parts/Models: bow section, forward hull, central hull, aft hull, stern, underwater hull, black lower-hull band, and white upper-hull structure. The red underwater hull occupies the lowest continuous portion; the black lower hull sits directly above it; the white upper hull rises cleanly above the black band. Do not include an interior, cutaway rooms, entry points, gangways, or playable deck circulation. Frame the complete vessel in an elevated three-quarter side view, with sufficient negative space to read its full 500-stud length and bow-to-stern proportions.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: the authoritative first image is an isometric showcase render because the visual silhouette, proportions, surface segmentation, and presentation of one display object lead the work.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge, driven by the approximately 500-stud overall length. Theme: historically inspired early-20th-century luxury ocean liner, clean editable model presentation, black/red/white hull livery. Use `SET` because this is real model geometry that nobody walks on; skip traversal and jump-gap checks.
